conviction_note: The evidence nets to roughly zero. The company restated its FY26 $220-230M guide on Nov 5, after Q3 had closed and October was known, which makes a Q3 miss against the $63-64M guide unlikely. Against that, a company that habitually advertises record months has cited nothing newer than July's $20.9M for over three months, and Meta's US ad prices rose. The stock slid 17% into the print with no company news and a non-crowded short (2.6% of shares, 2.8 days), and the last beat-and-raise (Q2) closed +0.15% on the day. p_up stays at 50 and abs_move_pct is 8 from 73.8% realised vol on a thin, sold-down name with no usable chain; impact_sum -0.5 and impact_scaled 0 disagree only by the small net negative of the silence and CAC items.

EPS consensus -$0.73. FY26 street $211.8M vs guide $220-230M (stale, below guide); FY27 street ~$359M vs company $400M+. Bar is sourced to the company guide and two agreeing estimate sources.

Without that, the July $20.9M is the last datapoint and the 17% slide says the market already doubts that momentum held.

next_guide.basis: In 2026 the company raised at every update (Q1 prelim to $190-210M, July 14 to $210-220M with a June prelim, Aug 18 to $220-230M). On Nov 5, with Q3 closed and October done, it restated $220-230M without the pre-announced raise it made in July. So maintain is most likely; a cut would contradict a two-week-old statement, and a raise is possible but was not signalled.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-05, after Q3 had closed and October was known, the company restated FY26 guidance of $220-230M and FY27 IM8 guidance of $400M+ in the Care Bears release. It had pre-announced a raise in July when it had a strong month in hand, and this time it did not. Read: Q3 lands inside the $63-64M guide (consensus $63.2M) and the FY guide is maintained, not raised.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last guide raise (Q2, 2026-08-18) to $220-230M plus a first FY27 guide closed +0.15% that session and drifted to about -3% to -4% over the next two days (baseline rows 08-18 and 08-20; Simply Wall St -3.3%).
findings.why_not_priced: The restatement sat inside a licensing PR and was not reported as a reaffirmation. If the market had read it as removing miss risk, the stock would not have fallen a further ~4% from $16.12 on Nov 5 to $15.43 into the print. Street FY26 ($211.8M) still sits below the low end of the guide.
findings.independence: The Aug 20 Lily Collins release (https://finviz.com/news/384189/prenetics-im8-announces-two-time-golden-globe-nominated-actress-and-producer-lily-collins-as-im8-global-ambassador-and-shareholder-in-multi-year-partnership) said adjusted FCF was expected to stay positive for the full Q3. That is an earlier in-quarter statement, from a different document, pointing the same way.

findings.finding: The company advertised record months as they happened: Oct 2025 $9M in a standalone PR, May 2026 $16.7M, a June 2026 preliminary $17M, July 2026 $20.9M. Every release since Aug 18 (Aug 20, Nov 3, Nov 5) still cites July's $20.9M as the latest month. No August, September or October record has been announced, although the $300M exit run-rate needs ~$25M a month by December.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Monthly-record PRs have been how this name communicates momentum. The baseline's 6-K rows (e.g. 08-26 +10.88) are partly such updates, not prints.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference from silence, so it is partly priced: the 17% 20-day slide and the Nov 10 preview headline ('must prove July's record momentum held') show the market is already asking. If a new record month had been disclosed, the preview would have quoted it, and the stock would not sit 60% below the mean target.
findings.independence: The Nov 3 CFO release (https://finviz.com/news/414338/prenetics-im8-names-brian-j-rosin-as-successor-chief-financial-officer) also gave no monthly figure. Precedent for advertising records: the Oct 2025 PR (https://finviz.com/news/216508/prenetics-im8-achieves-record-9-million-in-revenue-for-october-surpasses-108-million-in-annualized-recurring-revenue-11-months-after-launch). This finding shares the Nov 5 document with the reaffirmation finding but reads a different thing from it (what is absent, not what is restated). The two are consistent: in line, no upside.

findings.finding: Expectations are already low. Spot $15.43 is down 17.2% over 20 days and 10.5% over 5 days with no company-specific negative news found, sits 41% below the 52-week high and about 60% below the mean target of $38.89, and short interest is low and flat (2.6% of shares, 2.8 days). An in-line Q3 with an October run-rate datapoint clears a lower bar than the consensus number implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's guide raise into a ~10% 30-day decline produced no relief rally (+0.15%, then -4.21% on 08-20).
findings.why_not_priced: Not 'unpriced'. This is a statement about where the price already sits. The cause of the drawdown is unexplained, so it may itself be information (informed selling on consumer data) rather than a mispricing.
findings.independence: Targets: https://fintel.io/s/us/PRE. Short interest: https://equibles.com/stocks/pre/shortinterest. Price path: the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: Meta's Q3 2026 average price per ad rose 14% year on year globally (23% in US & Canada per one source), with impressions up 10%. IM8 acquires customers through paid social: it guided H2 marketing at a similar or slightly better share of revenue than Q2, did not build July's $239 CAC into guidance, and Q2 CAC was $301.
findings.link: Meta is IM8's ad-channel supplier: ~95% of IM8 sales are its own DTC site, acquisition spend was $36.2M in Q2, and the company's own release describes IM8 'accelerating TikTok and Meta expansion' (https://finviz.com/news/359626/prenetics-appoints-hudson-leogrande-founder-and-ceo-of-multi-billion-dollar-dtc-brand-comfrt-to-board-of-directors-as-im8-accelerates-tiktok-and-meta-expansion). The share of spend on Meta is not disclosed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CAC/EBITDA has not been the line on which this stock reacted; the Q2 EBITDA loss of ~$19M as marketing doubled drew little reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: No PRE preview links Meta's Q3 ad pricing to IM8's CAC; the Nov 10 preview names CAC drift back to ~$300 as the risk without a source for it. It is a proxy: Meta attributes the higher prices partly to better conversion, which could offset the cost for an advertiser.
findings.independence: Meta's own Q3 release (https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Meta-Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Results/) carries the 14% figure. The US 23% is single-source (merca20). No IM8-specific confirmation.

findings.finding: The Q3 bar is the company's own guide. Consensus revenue of $63.2-63.3M sits at the low end of the $63-64M guide, unlike Q2, when consensus ($48.8M) sat above the $46-48M guide and the company printed $46.5M inside its guide but 5% under the street. The prior pattern of consensus misses came from the street running above the guide, and that gap is gone.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2: inside guide, below consensus, stock +0.15% on the day. Q3 2025: revenue miss vs consensus, stock reaction not found.
findings.why_not_priced: This lands inside what the company guided, so it is largely priced. The only point is that a headline 'revenue miss' is less likely this time than on the last two prints.
findings.independence: The Q3 guide is from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15463847119635456); the Q3 consensus from https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/PRE/earnings-forecasts.

findings.finding: Q3 is the first full quarter under the up-to-$1B General Catalyst CVF facility, which funds up to 70% of monthly acquisition spend and is booked as a liability with the return as interest below operating income. The 'positive consolidated adjusted FCF' the company promised for Q3 includes those financing inflows.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The facility was announced 2026-07-14 alongside a guide raise; the isolated reaction was not found.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the Nov 10 preview already flags that the FCF figure includes facility proceeds. What the money buys is visible customer acquisition (118k customers added in Q2, 140k active subscribers, July cohort 47k), so it funds demand rather than distress. Sized at zero.
findings.independence: The Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15463847119635456) has the CFO warning the arrangement 'may not function as expected'.

findings.finding: The group CFO change was announced 2026-11-03, two weeks before the print: Stephen Lo hands over to Brian Rosin (who joined in May as IM8 CFO) effective 2026-12-31, and finance moves to the US. Described as planned; Lo stays on as Senior Advisor.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline shows -7.26% on 2026-11-02 and -1.7% on 11-03 around the announcement window. Cause not confirmed; the 11-02 move predates the release.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced; the stock already fell around it. Residual risk: a departing CFO weeks before a print can precede conservative guidance or accounting changes. Nothing found supports that.

findings.finding: Sell-side flow into the print: three Buy initiations in two months (Craig-Hallum $40 on 09-17, Lucid $54 on 10-12, Maxim $41 on 10-26). AAII reports one unidentified analyst downgrade as of 2026-11-16, with no broker named and none found elsewhere (possibly a quant rating).
findings.why_not_priced: The downgrade, if real, falls inside the 5-day slide and is priced. The initiations are old news.
findings.independence: Fintel lists no rating change Sept-Nov (https://fintel.io/s/us/PRE), which contradicts AAII's downgrade or means it was a non-broker rating.

findings.finding: Insiders have been buying: the CEO and CFO bought $1.0M of shares in the open market after Q2 results, bringing insider buying since Nov 2025 to $3.75M. No insider sales were found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline shows +10.88% on 2026-08-26, around the date of the insider-buy announcement.
findings.why_not_priced: Old and public; the stock has fallen through the purchase price since. Small confirmation that management was not sitting on bad Q3 news in late August.

outside_window.finding: Care Bears by IM8: a 10-year exclusive Authentic Brands licence, kids/adult gummies launching 1H 2027. Not in the 2026 or 2027 guides. Authentic becomes a strategic shareholder; share count and price not disclosed.
The IM8 Hydration launch is guided for Q4 2026 and is not in guidance. Its revenue cannot show in the Q3 print, though launch commentary may come on the call.
